  "policy_quotes": {
    "42": "Version 2.0 (October 20, 2026) — version history",
    "45": "This document describes NLnet Foundation's policy on the use of GenAI — including large language models, diffusion models and code assistants — in applications submitted to NLnet and in all work delivered within NLnet-funded grants. It covers both the application process and the execution of funded activities. The policy exclusively concerns GenAI and does not regulate other forms of automation.",
    "48": "It is not allowed to use generative AI during the writing of proposals, nor when providing answers during the interactive evaluation of proposals. This includes LLM generation of ideas, as well as restructuring, shortening and translation. Trust in your knowledge and skills, and use your own words. We don't care about spelling or grammar, only about your ideas.",
    "49": "Accessibility exception: there is one noted exception where using AI in the application process is allowed, which is in case it is needed for accessibility purposes. People with e.g. a visual or motor impairment who rely on AI-based assistive technology are allowed to use AI. Like any other use of AI, it must always be made transparent. Instructions on how to disclose use of AI when submitting proposals are provided in the proposal form.",
    "50": "In your application you must disclose if your proposal builds on an existing codebase that already includes a significant amount of code generated by AI, or expects to gain a significant amount of such code during the lifetime in other ways than through the grant. Please also note the recommendations found below on transparency.",
    "52": "It is not allowed to use generative AI for producing artefacts of any kind, including code, design, and documentation.",
    "53": "It is allowed to employ GenAI in a read-only manner — meaning, for instance, that you can have an AI tool check your code and identify security issues and flaws, but that you craft fixes and mitigations yourself, and write your own code. Even if you use GenAI in a read-only manner, you should always be transparent about it.",
    "54": "Technology does not replace human responsibility for project quality, technical choices and thoroughness. Human contributors remain responsible for correctness, clarity, and reproducibility, and are expected to understand and be able to explain design and code decisions.",
    "55": "Costs incurred for AI usage are not eligible for reimbursement.",
    "67": "We have a dedicated FAQ for the GenAI policy. This includes the transitional arrangement for NGI Zero projects."
  },
  "applicability": "The published policy expressly covers proposals submitted to NLnet and funded artifacts. It refers to an NGI Zero transition FAQ. No exception for this proposed workflow was established by this assessment.",
  "reopen": "First-party call-specific terms expressly permitting this workflow, or a separately evidenced eligible human-led application and delivery plan complying with the operative policy and disclosing existing AI-generated code as required.",
